summary: Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who completed her doctorate under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2006). She held positions at the University of Vienna (~2012–2017), the IKGA (~2017–2022), and became Associate Professor at the University of Toronto (~2022).

Elisa Ganser works in Indology and philosophy. Her appointments include serving as Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026) and as a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza studied theology at the Universities of Würzburg (1958–1962) and Münster (~1963–1970). She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (appointed 1988).

Working in Indology, religious studies, and archaeology, Elizabeth A. Cecil earned degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University (PhD 2008). She taught at Leiden University (~2016–2018) before joining Florida State University as Assistant Professor (~2018).

Elizabeth De Michelis studied at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (PhD ~1998–2002). Working in Indology and religious studies, she directed the Dharam Hinduja Institute of Indic Research (2000) and held posts at the Universities of Cambridge and Oxford.

Elizabeth English is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford in 1999 under the doctoral supervision of Alexis Sanderson, having also studied under Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington studied at SOAS and completed graduate work under Adrian David Hugh Bivar. Specializing in archaeology and Buddhist studies, she served as curator of pre-Islamic coins of South and Central Asia at the British Museum from 1993.

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Canterbury in 1994. Her academic career includes serving as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris earned her doctorate from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and University of Kelaniya (~1988–1993). Working in Buddhist and religious studies, she held posts at Westminster College (attested 1996) and University of Birmingham (~2015).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in Sinology and history who completed her studies at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978). She subsequently held academic appointments at the University of Washington (~1978–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and Sinology, having completed her doctorate under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She held an instructor post at Amherst College (1998–1999) and an appointment at Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner. A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She was appointed Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006) under the supervision of Thomas B. Larsson and Bozena Werbart, alongside co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. Her career includes posts at the Kern Institute (attested 2003) and on an editorial board at Leiden University (attested 2018).
Elliot M. Stern is an Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, earning PhD degrees attested in 1988 and 1998.

Elliot Sperling studied at Queens College and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD ~1980–1983). A specialist in Tibetology and history, he taught at the University of Southern Mississippi, served as Associate Professor at Indiana University (1987–2015), and was Professor at Harvard (1992–1993).

Ellison Banks Findly works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held posts at Mount Holyoke College as well as Trinity College, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).

Emanuel Sarkisyanz studied at the University of Tehran (~1943–1945) and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1948–1952). A scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he became Head at Heidelberg University in 1967.
Emanuela Garatti is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).
